record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: For weights on [0,1] of the form w(x)=∏_i |Q_i(x)|^{α_i} with polynomial factors Q_i and nonnegative exponents α_i, determine the infimum of the quantity -2 log(capacity_w([0,1]))/α+1 over all such weights. If the infimum equals 1, exhibit a sequence of weights achieving that value asymptotically; if it is strictly larger than 1, determine whether the infimum is attained by a weight of this form.

evidence.quote: QUESTION 8.1. For w(x) as in (8.3) ... find ... If κ = 1 then find a sequence of weights that gives this value. If κ ≠ 1 then investigate whether κ is attained for a weight of the form (8.3).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider weights on the interval [0,1] of the form
  w(x) = ∏_{i=1}^k |Q_i(x)|^{α_i},
where each Q_i is a polynomial with integer coefficients (not identically zero) and each α_i is a nonnegative real number. Set α = ∑_{i=1}^k α_i · deg(Q_i).

For such a weight w, let cap_w([0,1]) denote the weighted logarithmic capacity of [0,1] with external field −log w; equivalently, cap_w([0,1]) = exp(−F_w), where F_w = inf_μ ∫∫ log(1/|x−y|) dμ(x) dμ(y) − 2 ∫ log w(x) dμ(x), with the infimum taken over Borel probability measures μ supported on [0,1].

Define
  κ = inf_w  (−2 log cap_w([0,1])) / (α + 1),
where the infimum is taken over all weights w of the above form (with α > 0).

(a) Determine the value of κ.
(b) If κ = 1, exhibit an explicit sequence of admissible weights w_n for which the ratio (−2 log cap_{w_n}([0,1])) / (α(w_n) + 1) tends to 1.
(c) If κ > 1, decide whether the infimum is attained by some weight w of the prescribed form, and if so, describe such an extremal weight.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem arises in the Gelfond–Schnirelman approach to prime number theory via weighted potential theory on [0,1]. Searches turned up extensive work by Totik and others on weighted equilibrium problems and the Gelfond–Schnirelman method, but no resolution determining the infimum κ or whether κ = 1 (which would yield the prime number theorem by this method). The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Gelfond–Schnirelman Method in Prime Number Theory
status_evidence.snippet: A lower bound for the integral of Chebyshev's ψ-function is given in terms of weighted capacity; the Gelfond–Schnirelman method uses polynomials with integer coefficients of small norm on [0,1].
status_evidence.claim: The infimum κ governing the Gelfond–Schnirelman approach via weighted polynomial capacity on [0,1] is studied; whether κ=1 is not established.

status_evidence.title: Weighted Approximation with Varying Weight (Totik)
status_evidence.snippet: Weighted polynomial approximation and weighted equilibrium problems are extensively developed, but no determination of the infimum for polynomial weights with integer coefficients on [0,1] is given.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on weighted potential theory do not resolve the value of κ for this class of weights.
